headline: A 2019 law makes a technical fix so a pay rule for certain Senate Restaurants workers no longer applies to their retirement benefits.
what_it_does: Some Senate Restaurants employees used to work for the Architect of the Capitol (AOC) and later became employees of a contractor under a food services contract. A rule treated their basic pay rate as the same as the rate when AOC signed that contract. This law says that rule no longer applies when figuring their retirement benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Certain former Architect of the Capitol employees who now work at Senate Restaurants through a food services contractor
who_it_affects.how: Their retirement benefits are no longer calculated using the older pay rate that was set when AOC entered into the contract.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that administer retirement benefits for these workers
who_it_affects.how: They must calculate these benefits without the pay-rate rule that the law removes.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on June 12, 2019.
